# tenferro v0.12.0

`main` carried the `0.11.0` version string for the 107 commits after `cef3746f`,
the commit the published 0.11.0 crates were built from, while the public surface
under it changed into the one call grammar of #2552. v0.12.0 renumbers that tree
and collects what those commits change. The version moves one minor because no
compatibility promise exists yet; a Rust caller should still read it as a
breaking release.

Read [`docs/getting-started/api-migration.md`](../../docs/getting-started/api-migration.md)
first. It carries the per-operation migration table, and
[`docs/spec/generated/api-ops.md`](../../docs/spec/generated/api-ops.md) is the
generated registry of every operation, its options type, its `_into` modes and
its declared omissions.

## Breaking changes

### One call grammar per operation family

Every family (core, linalg, einsum, FFT) now has one spelling per layer, built on
a per-family registry ([#2552](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2552),
merged as [#2580](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2580); the eager
`EagerSession` surface is
[#2603](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2603)):

```text
recv.op(operands…, exec)                     // concrete, default options
recv.op_with(operands…, &opts, exec)         // concrete, explicit XxxOptions
recv.op_into(operands…, [&opts,] exec, dest) // concrete, only where declared
session.op(&x, operands…)                    // eager: the session is the receiver
traced.op_with(operands…, &opts)             // traced: no exec
```

The engine is always the last concrete argument, and a concrete receiver is any
`AsView` value (`Tensor`, `TensorRead`, `TypedTensor<T>`, `TypedTensorView<T>` or
a reference to one), so typed inputs return typed results from the same method.

What is gone, and where the replacement is:

- The per-receiver linalg, einsum, tensordot, FFT and session-ops extension
  traits (`TensorLinalgExt`, `TensorReadLinalgExt`, `TypedTensorLinalgExt`,
  `TracedTensorLinalgExt`, `TraceContextLinalgExt`, `EagerSessionLinalgExt`,
  `EagerTensorLinalgExt`, the einsum and tensordot extensions, the six FFT
  extensions, and `TensorSessionOpsExt` / `TypedTensorSessionOpsExt` /
  `TypedTensorMaskSessionOpsExt`). `CoreOps` (tenferro-runtime), `LinalgOps`,
  `TracedLinalgOps`, `EagerLinalgOps`, `EinsumOps`, `TensordotOps`,
  `TracedEinsumOps`, `TracedTensordotOps`, `EagerEinsumOps`, `FftOps`,
  `TracedFftOps` and `EagerFftOps` replace them.
- Every `*_read` spelling (`svd_read`, `einsum_read_into`, `fft_read`, …): pass
  the `TensorRead` to the plain method.
- `svd_full`, `*_with_options`, `pinv_with_rtol`, `solve_read_into`,
  `dot_general_with_conj`, positional `triangular_solve`/`norm` arguments,
  `einsum_notation`/`einsum_subscripts`, the positional `FftExecutor` entries and
  the six free `*_with_exec` linalg functions. Each has a named replacement in
  the migration table.
- An operation has an `XxxOptions` type and an `_with` form only when it has
  semantic options; `add`, `solve`, `lstsq`, `householder_qr`, `lu`,
  `full_piv_lu`, `full_piv_lu_solve`, `eig`, `eigvals`, `slogdet`, `det`, `inv`
  and `tensordot` have none, so their `_into` forms take no options either
  ([#2580](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2580)).

Backend and provider hooks (`Engine::{svd_read,…}`, `TensorDot`,
`LinalgBackend`, `FftBackend`) are provider contracts and are unchanged.

### Results are structs, and `_into` writes into a `Dest`

`Svd { u, s, vh }`, `Qr { q, r }`, `Lu { p, l, u, parity }`,
`FullPivLu { p, l, u, q, parity }`, `Eig { values, vectors }`,
`Eigh { values, vectors }` and `Slogdet { sign, log_abs_det }` replace the tuples
and the `TypedSvd`/`TypedLu`/`TypedFullPivLu`/`TypedEig` aliases; fields keep the
former tuple order, so a caller that took the result apart positionally names
those fields now.

`_into` writes into `tenferro_tensor::Dest` (`Dest::overwrite`,
`Dest::accumulate`, `Dest::scaled(out, alpha, beta)`) and exists only where the
registry declares it: `add_into`, `solve_into`, `einsum_into` and
`ConcreteEinsumPlan::execute_into`. An undeclared mode is `Unsupported` before
any write.

### Axes are `isize`, and lanes replace the `*_with_exec` entries

Public axis arguments (`CoreOps`, `TracedTensor`, `EagerSession`, linalg `norm`,
FFT options, `TensorDotAxes::Axes`) are `isize`, and a negative axis counts from
the end; `AxisVec`, `normalize_axis` and `normalize_axes` are public and
`AxisOutOfBounds.axis` is `isize`. IR-shaped configurations and
`broadcast_in_dim` keep `usize`.

`CpuEngine::with_lanes(&shares, &mut pools, |i, lane| ..)` splits the engine's
thread budget into lanes, each with a caller-owned `BufferPool` (re-exported at
the `tenferro-cpu` root), and replaces the six `*_with_exec` entries: inside a
lane the ordinary grammar runs (`view.svd(lane)`). Only `svd`, `svdvals`, `qr`,
`eigh`, `eigvalsh` and `eigvals` run in a lane; every other operation returns
`Unsupported`.

### The vendor BLAS/LAPACK CPU providers are gone

Every build now links one faer-backed `tlinalg`/`cpueinsum`/`tcontract` stack
([#2608](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/issues/2608), merged as
[#2609](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2609)). The features
`native`, `blas`, `blas-openblas`, `blas-mkl`, `blas-accelerate`,
`provider-inject`, `provider-src`, `cpueinsum-blas` and `tlinalg-blas` no longer
exist on `tenferro-cpu`, `tenferro-linalg`, `tenferro-runtime`, `tenferro-ad`,
`tenferro-einsum`, `tenferro-fft`, `tenferro-gpu`, `tenferro-xla` or
`docs/tutorial-code`; there is no back-compat alias, so a stale dependency line
fails with "feature does not exist". `tenferro-cpu` and `tenferro-runtime` no
longer declare a `default` feature, because `default` *was* the provider
selector, and `tenferro-runtime` declares no features at all.

Migration: delete the feature name and the `default-features = false` that went
with it. `cblas-sys`, `cblas-inject`, `blas-src`, `lapack`, `lapack-src` and
`lapack-inject` are no longer workspace dependencies, so `openblas-src`,
`openblas-build`, `intel-mkl-src` and `accelerate-src` leave `Cargo.lock`.

### Smaller removals

- `TensorBackendCapability::require_capability` is gone; the descriptor is a
  declaration, not a gate, and every backend already refuses a pair it cannot
  serve in its own dispatch
  ([#2477](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/issues/2477), merged as
  [#2619](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2619)). Read a
  declaration with `capability()` / `capability_entry()` and let the engine
  refuse execution.
- Eight unused internal `pub` items are gone
  ([#2546](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/issues/2546)):
  `ShapeGuardContext` loses `refresh_global_metadata`,
  `with_extension_ad_dispatcher`, `set_transpose_primal_outputs`,
  `transpose_primal_outputs`, `transpose_primal_outputs_were_used`,
  `take_deferred_shape_error` and `extend_metadata`, and `CudaEngine` loses
  `runtime_mut`.

### Dependency moves

| dependency | 0.11.0 | 0.12.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `cpueinsum-blas`, `tlinalg-blas` | 0.12.0 / 0.5.1 | removed |
| `cblas-sys`, `cblas-inject`, `blas-src`, `lapack`, `lapack-src`, `lapack-inject` | present | removed |
| `t4a-cuda-runtime` | `=0.1.0` (rev `a1fd7ae`) | `=0.1.1` (rev `147af9e`) |

`tlinalg` 0.11.0, `cpueinsum` 0.12.0, `tcontract-exec` 0.12.0, the `strided-*`
0.12.0 line, `threadteam` 0.5.1, `t4a-faer` 0.33.0 and `t4a-cuda-kernels` 0.1.2
are unchanged. `scripts/check-single-versions.sh` is the check that keeps one
identity per crate in the resolved graph.

## New

### `tenferro-mpi` and `tenferro-hdf5`

Two optional adapters moved from `ext/` into the root workspace
([#2621](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2621)), with empty
default features so the root lanes need neither MPI nor HDF5.

- `tenferro-mpi` moves one host tensor between two ranks over MPI
  point-to-point messages — `send`, `recv` and `recv_into` for `TypedTensor` and
  the dtype-erased `Tensor`
  ([#2617](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2617)). It borrows the
  caller's communicator and never initializes or finalizes MPI. A `Gpu` tensor
  does not implement `Transport`, so a device transfer is a compile error.
  Opt in with `system` (needs MPI headers and libclang) or `runtime` (loads MPI
  at run time); the two are mutually exclusive.
- `tenferro-hdf5` stores host tensors in HDF5 datasets through caller-supplied
  handles, with a versioned schema and no hidden transfer or conversion
  ([#2611](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2611), merged as
  [#2615](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2615)). Opt in with
  `hdf5`.

### Two engine hooks

- `CpuEngine::dispatch_costs` returns the `threadteam::DispatchCosts` the
  engine's tokens use, so a caller can decide with `num_threads` and
  `width_for_by` / `pays_at` whether an operation would fork before taking a
  token ([#2590](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2590)).
- `CpuEngine::with_guard` is `with_exec` at width one minus the placement token:
  the same refusal of a broken engine, the same unwind handling and the same
  workspace retention bound, but no worker is reserved
  ([#2591](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2591)).
- `EighOptions::batch_policy` says how many cuSOLVER launches a batch may cost.
  `EighBatchPolicy::RequireBatched` turns the silent per-matrix fallback into a
  typed `Unsupported` error naming the missing symbol and the fallback it
  declined; the default keeps 0.11.0's routing unchanged
  ([#2622](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2622)).

## Fixes

- A one-input `stack` / `concatenate` compiles. `StdTensorOp::Concatenate` read
  the output dtype from inputs 0 and 1, so one input failed in shape inference
  and inputs past the second were ignored; the dtype now folds over every input
  ([#2599](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2599), merged as
  [#2600](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2600)).
- `EinsumOptimize::False` contracts left to right again, instead of building
  pair intermediates the notation never mentions. On `"ij,jk,kl,lm,m->i"`
  (d=256, f64, serial engine) step 3 was a 256³ outer product, 128 MiB of
  intermediate and 186.9 ms, against 3.33 ms for the documented order.
- A traced `tensordot` axis of `isize::MIN` panicked in overflow-checked
  builds instead of reporting `AxisOutOfBounds`, because `normalize_axis`
  computed `rank + axis` before the bound check. The explicit-axis path now
  uses the shared `tenferro_tensor::normalize_axis`
  ([#2605](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/issues/2605), merged as
  [#2606](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2606)).
- Eager `lstsq` refuses a rank-deficient `A` instead of returning a solution
  ([#2583](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/issues/2583), merged as
  [#2584](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2584)).
- `norm` documents its `ord = 0` NaN contract on the public surface
  ([#2626](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/issues/2626), merged as
  [#2627](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2627)).
- `CpuEngine`'s cache controls cover its extension cache store:
  `runtime_cache_stats` adds the store's entries and retained bytes,
  `clear_runtime_caches` clears it, and `take_extension_caches` moves the store
  out instead of allocating an empty one
  ([#2587](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2587), merged as
  [#2588](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2588)).

## Results that can differ in the final bit

- CUDA softplus is one fused launch on `F32`/`F64`
  ([#2530](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2530)). It computes the
  composite's arithmetic through the same device helpers and picks the same
  operand the composite's compare-and-select picks, so a non-NaN input gives the
  composite's bits; a NaN input stays NaN, possibly with a different sign or
  payload.
- The `EinsumOptimize::False` fix above changes the summation order, so results
  can differ in the last bits from 0.11.0 while matching the same order written
  as an explicit `EinsumOptimize::Path`.

## Known limitations

- A lane runs six factorizations and returns `Unsupported` for everything else;
  every operation outside `with_lanes` keeps the ordinary grammar.
- `tenferro-hdf5` stays `publish = false` until `hdf5-rt` is on crates.io, so it
  is a workspace crate, not a crates.io package, in this release.
- `tenferro-mpi` is publishable but has never been published; its first
  publication needs the release owner's per-package approval.

**Full comparison:** https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/compare/tenferro-tensor-v0.11.0...main
— the 0.11.0 crates were published from `cef3746f` under per-crate
`tenferro-*-v0.11.0` tags; a `v0.12.0` tag narrows this to the release commit.
